description: Guided, reproducible experiments for learning how modelling choices affect results. Results should be produced by the app or notebook, not prefilled as measured facts.

experiments.title: Baseline vs. Complex Model
experiments.question: Does a more complex model outperform a simple baseline on unseen data?
procedure: Create a fixed train/test split.
Train a mean-prediction baseline.
Train linear regression and a decision tree.
Compare train and test MAE.
experiments.expected_learning: A complex model may fit training data better but generalize worse.
experiments.deliverable: Comparison table and a two-sentence conclusion.

experiments.title: Learning Rate Sweep
experiments.question: How does the learning rate affect convergence speed and stability?
procedure: Choose at least four learning rates.
Use the same model initialization and data split.
Record the loss after each epoch.
Plot learning rate against final loss and convergence behaviour.
experiments.expected_learning: Very low rates can converge slowly; high rates may oscillate or diverge.
experiments.deliverable: Loss plot and a justified learning-rate choice.

experiments.title: Feature Ablation Study
experiments.question: Which input features contribute useful predictive signal?
procedure: Train a model with all permitted features.
Remove one feature group at a time.
Repeat each configuration with fixed folds.
Compare validation scores and variability.
experiments.expected_learning: A feature can be redundant, noisy, or useful only in combination with other features.

experiments.title: Regularization and Generalization
experiments.question: How does regularization strength change training and validation performance?
procedure: Fit a model with weak regularization.
Evaluate a logarithmic range of alpha values.
Plot train and validation error.
Choose a value using validation data only.
experiments.expected_learning: Stronger regularization can reduce overfitting but may eventually cause underfitting.
experiments.deliverable: Error curve and selected alpha with rationale.

experiments.title: Accuracy Under Class Imbalance
experiments.question: Can accuracy hide poor performance on a rare class?
procedure: Generate datasets with different minority-class fractions.
Train the same baseline model.
Evaluate all four metrics.
Inspect the confusion matrix at each class balance.
experiments.expected_learning: Accuracy can remain high while minority-class recall is poor.
experiments.deliverable: Metric comparison and recommendation for a suitable metric.

experiments.title: Classification Threshold Trade-off
experiments.question: How does changing a probability threshold affect precision and recall?
experiments.dataset: Binary classification dataset with predicted probabilities
procedure: Train one classifier and preserve its test probabilities.
Evaluate thresholds from 0.1 to 0.9.
Plot precision and recall against the threshold.
Choose a threshold for a stated error-cost scenario.
experiments.expected_learning: Threshold selection changes error trade-offs without retraining the model.
experiments.deliverable: Threshold plot and a decision linked to the use case.

record_schema.rule: Record actual run outputs; do not fabricate metric values.
